metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Presents RB2 Value in Week 5
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson has RB2 upside in a Week 5 clash with the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers are No. 23 against opposing running backs in fantasy, allowing 21.73 points per game. Wilson has looked solid in the two games in which he received heavy volume. Additionally, he was a true workhorse in Week 4, racking up 21 carries and four targets. His two touchdowns led to a 27-point fantasy outing. With Jadarian Price (chest) on IR and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still at least a week away from returning to the lineup, Wilson's role should remain unchanged. The 49ers are allowing big receiving totals to opposing running backs (51.8 yards per game on 7.8 receptions), which bodes well for PPR fantasy managers. Seattle will also almost certainly try to control this game on the ground, suggesting that Wilson will push for 20-plus carries once again; not to mention, Wilson should receive a goal line carry or two. Start Wilson with confidence this weekend.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson A High-Volume Buy-Low Target Ahead of Week 5
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson assumed the role of the clear workhorse RB1 in his team's offense in Week 4, and rewarded fantasy managers with a 27.0 PPR fantasy point game thanks to a massive volume of touches. He carried the ball 21 times for 81 yards and one touchdown and caught three of his four targets for 29 yards and another score in the game. This level of volume for any RB in a good offense can't be ignored. While the return of RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) is imminent, he's coming back from an ACL injury, and he may take several weeks to ramp back up to full participation in practice and start meaningfully eating into Wilson's workload. The Seahawks teased the signing of veteran RB Joe Mixon, but opted against it after a physical, meaning Wilson will be set up as the RB1 for the next few weeks. The impending return of Charbonnet will certainly lower Wilson's fantasy trade value, meaning he can be had for much cheaper than his scoring upside would suggest, making him a recommended buy-low target for fantasy football ahead of Week 5.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Breaks Out as Lead Back with Charbonnet and Price Out
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson had 21 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown, along with three receptions for 39 yards and another score in the 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. In his first start of the season, Wilson went off, scoring a career-high 25.5 half-PPR fantasy points in Week 4. With rookie running back Jadarian Price (chest) and Zach Charbonnet (knee) on injured reserve, Wilson became the clear starter, playing 60% of snaps and taking 76% of backfield opportunities. With no timetable for Charbonnet's return and Price out until at least Week 8, Wilson should be the lead back in the coming weeks. Fantasy managers should add Wilson on waivers, as he's an RB2 with both Charbonnet and Price out.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson scores twice Sunday
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson ran for 81 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards receiving and another score.
metadata.analysis: After a fumble on a muffled punt by the Chargers early, Wilson took a screen pass from Sam Darnold to the house for the first score of the day. He was the clear workhorse in the first game since Jadarian Price was placed on IR.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - Turns in 120 total yards
metadata.description: Wilson racked up 21 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown and added three catches (on four targets) for 39 yards and another TD during Sunday's 30-23 win versus the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: In the wake of Jadarian Price's placement on injured reserve due to a chest issue, Wilson got the first chance to pace the Seahawks backfield, and he parlayed the second-highest touch count of his career into his second ever outing with 100-plus yards from scrimmage and his second two-TD performance. Meanwhile, fellow RB George Holani received eight touches, which he turned into 20 total yards. Until Zach Charbonnet (knee, reserve/PUP list) is able to return to action, Wilson figures to be Seattle's lead runner.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Scores a Pair of Touchdowns in Workhorse Role
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson totaled 21 carries, 81 rushing yards, three catches, 39 receiving yards, and two touchdowns during Sunday's Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Wilson stepped up as the Seahawks' every-down back after Jadarian Price (chest) was placed on injured reserve. He has now logged 20+ carries in two of his last three games, and he has proven to be very capable of handling a large workload. It will be interesting to see how this backfield shakes out going forward. On one hand, we have no doubt that Wilson could lead the way and rank as a fringe RB2 in fantasy football. On the other hand, the Seahawks have been linked to free agent running back Joe Mixon as a potential Price replacement, and projected No. 1 running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) is eligible to return from injured reserve as early as this upcoming week. Wilson has some short-term appeal in redraft leagues, but his floor will drop pretty quickly once Charbonnet returns to action.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Getting First-Team Reps in Warmups
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson appears set to get the start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. Corbin K. Smith reported that Wilson took the first running back reps during pregame warmups with Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve. Wilson has 32 carries for 109 yards through three games, with most of that production coming in a 21-carry, 92-yard performance against Arizona in Week 2. George Holani is also available and figures to see work, but Wilson getting the first reps before kickoff points to him opening the game atop the backfield.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson's Long-Term Value Surging Amid Backfield Injuries in Seattle
metadata.description: Three games into the 2026 season, Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson has recorded 32 carries for 109 yards. The 27-year-old has had his usage scaled up of late, leading Seattle in carries each of the team's last two games. With the news on Saturday that the Seahawks have placed rookie running back Jadarian Price (chest) on Injured Reserve with a chest injury, Wilson now looks like the clear lead back in Seattle. Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) is eligible to come off the Physically Unable to Perform list in Week 5, so Wilson's time as his team's RB1 could be short-lived. Still, with Price now sidelined through at least Week 7, Wilson should maintain a role in the Seahawks backfield even after Charbonnet returns. Wilson should be rostered in all fantasy formats and profiles as a solid flex option in Week 4.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson a Potential Flex Play in Week 4
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson is in line for a big role in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Seahawks will be without rookie running back Jadarian Price (chest), who picked up two DNPs to end the practice week. Wilson has been the preferred running back for carry volume behind Price throughout this season. Wilson has not been a particularly efficient runner this season, but he did manage 92 yards on 21 carries in Week 2 mop-up duty. Seattle figures to play from ahead for most of their matchup with the Chargers this weekend, which should provide Wilson with plenty of chances for touches. Wilson is unlikely to see much receiving volume this week, but he is the Seahawks' goal line back. As such, he should have a chance to fall into the end zone this weekend and accumulate decent yardage. He is a risky play because of his lack of passing game usage, but he will be the starting running back on a good offense this week. Wilson can be best viewed as a flex play in Week 4.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - In line for more work against Chargers
metadata.description: With Jadarian Price (chest) out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Wilson is expected to take on an expanded role out of the backfield, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson actually leads the Seahawks in carries (32) this season, but he's been splitting work with Price (28 carries) and George Holani (15) in what has been a three-man weave out of the backfield. Wilson is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry but could flirt with 20 rushing attempts Sunday, putting him very much in the fantasy RB2/3 mix.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Could Be In Line for Larger Role vs. Chargers in Week 4
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson could have an increased role against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4. Wilson appears to be fully healthy, while the rest of Seattle's backfield is dealing with various injuries. Rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest), who has had some struggles to begin his NFL career, logged a limited practice session on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday. Fellow running back George Holani (rib) was limited in practice both Thursday and Friday. Meanwhile, tailback Zach Charbonnet (knee), who tore his ACL in January, started the 2026 season on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list and returned to practice in a limited capacity this week, but will have to sit out the Week 4 game before he is eligible to return. Wilson and Holani led Seattle's running backs in snaps played with 24 in a Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders (Price played 19 snaps), but Wilson struggled with nine carries for 14 yards (1.6 yards per carry). He has rushed 32 times for 109 yards (3.4 yards per carry) without scoring yet in 2026. Still, he could have a starting role against the Chargers. Wilson is RotoBaller's No. 40 running back for Week 4, but he has a chance to outplay that ranking.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - Struggles as rusher vs. Washington
metadata.description: Wilson turned nine carries into 14 yards during the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson saw his role expand during the Seahawks' Week 2 win over the Cardinals after Jadarian Price left the game due to a chest injury, with the former finishing with 21 carries for 92 yards. Wilson returned to a rotational role with George Holani for Week 3 after Price was cleared to play, though Wilson actually led the backfield trio with nine carries, though six of those touches went for three yards or less. Wilson has 32 carries for 109 yards (3.4 YPC) through the first three games of the regular season, though it looks like the Seahawks may be shifting to a committee approach to the backfield instead of Price being the lead back. The Seahawks head back home for a Week 4 tilt against the Chargers this Sunday.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Remains a Priority Waiver-Wire Target Despite Quiet Week 3
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson had a rough game in his team's Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders, rushing for 14 yards on nine carries. However, Wilson's role in the crowded Seahawks backfield remains encouraging. Wilson led Seattle in backfield touches for the second straight week, and Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price coughed up a costly fumble that could lead to him falling down the depth chart. Wilson has only recorded one target across three games so far in 2026, so fantasy managers in PPR-scoring formats should expect limited upside from him as a receiver. Seattle could also get running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) back from Injured Reserve in the next couple of weeks, which would almost certainly impact Wilson's outlook. Still, Wilson looks like his team's preferred early-down and goal-line rusher for the time being, which makes him a must-add running back in most fantasy formats.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson quiet in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson rushed nine times for 14 yards in the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Wilson has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, recording less than 10 carries in two of three contests. The running back remains difficult to trust in a Seattle backfield with more questions than answers currently, with a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - Remaining as RB2 for Week 3
metadata.description: Wilson will be the Seahawks' RB2 for Sunday's game against the Commanders after Jadarian Price (chest) was cleared to play, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Wilson ended up logging 21 carries for 92 yards during the Seahawks' Week 2 win over the Cardinals, with most of those touches coming after Price left the game in the fourth quarter due to a chest injury. Price has been cleared to play against Washington, so Wilson and George Holani will provide backfield depth for Sunday's road tilt.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson a Worthy Stash in Week 3
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson received a surprise 21 carries in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. With Jadarian Price (chest) good to go in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders, Wilson's volume will certainly drop. However, he is an interesting player to watch as the Seahawks' running back room continues to shake out. The team seems to be moving away from George Holani as the No. 2 running back for the moment, and Wilson has often been on the field in short-yardage and goal line situations. While he is unlikely to have standalone value without an injury, Wilson is a potential bench stash as an insurance option in deeper leagues. The Commanders present as a good matchup for Seattle in Week 3, leaving the door open for some mop-up duty for Wilson as the game wears on.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson goes for 92 yards in win over Arizona
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson ran 21 times for 92 yards and failed to catch his only target in Seattle's 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson led the Seahawks backfield in the big win, out-touching Jadarian Price on the ground 21 to 13. He's a speculative add at best as the Seahawks continue to rotate running backs.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson a Priority Waiver-Wire Target with Teammate Injured
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson took on an enormous workload in Week 2, making him a high-priority waiver wire target for Week 3 and beyond. The Seahawks cruised to victory over the Cardinals, prompting them to run the ball 40 times as they looked to drain the clock. Wilson was a big part of that effort, rushing for 92 yards on 21 attempts. It's worth noting that Wilson's role did grow after Jadarian Price (chest) exited in the second half, but he was still well on his way to a substantial workload even before the rookie left the game. Price's status is something to consider when placing a claim for Wilson this week. It's evident the Seahawks want to get Wilson involved no matter what, but he'd likely only get 20+ touches again if Price were to miss a game. The 27-year-old doesn't have much receiving upside, but he's a high-volume running back with decent efficiency numbers and touchdown upside. He should be a priority waiver wire target in Week 3 with the potential to earn a spot in fantasy lineups right away.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - Notches 21 carries in victory
metadata.description: Wilson rushed 21 times for 92 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 31-7 win over Arizona.
metadata.analysis: Wilson stepped into a larger workload Week 2, partially due to rookie running back Jadarian Price exiting the game with a chest injury in the fourth quarter. The 92 rushing yards were Wilson's highest total since he notched 107 yards and two scores on 28 totes in Week 12 of the 2025 campaign while with the Packers. Wilson could handle the lion's share of touches in the backfield against the Commanders in Week 3 if Price is forced to miss the contest.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Buried on Seahawks Running Back Depth Chart
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson played a minimal role in his team's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots, recording two carries for three yards. With Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) on Injured Reserve at the start of the year, Wilson appeared to have a chance to carve out a role in the Seattle backfield. However, it was George Holani who played the complementary role to rookie Seahawks back Jadarian Price in Week 1. Wilson played just three snaps on offense against New England and appears to be buried on the depth chart in the RB3 role. An injury to either Price or Holani could potentially change the outlook for Wilson in the short term. Still, Charbonnet has reportedly been making progress and could return shortly after he is first eligible in Week 5. At this point, Wilson would likely need a change of scenery to get back on the radar of fantasy managers in redraft leagues.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson - Two touches in Seahawks debut
metadata.description: Wilson rushed twice for three yards and wasn't targeted in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Wilson worked as a distant third option in Seattle's backfield behind Jadarian Price (58 yards on 12 touches) and George Holani (29 yards on eight touches). As long as Price and Holani are healthy, Wilson is unlikely to get meaningful playing time, and Seattle's backfield could get even more crowded once Zach Charbonnet (knee) comes off the PUP list.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson uninvolved in win Wednesday
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson rushed the ball two times for three yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
metadata.analysis: There were many questions about Seattle's backfield split over the course of the offseason, and we finally got some answers on Wednesday. One of the takeaways is that Wilson is not likely to be a significant contributor in the rotation, as he saw just two out of the team's 20 RB rushing attempts on the night. It looks like Jadarian Price and George Holani have squarely established themselves as the top two backs on this team, with Wilson being a distant third.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) off injury report Wednesday
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson is off the injury report for Wednesday's game against the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Wilson practiced in full all week. He'll be in a depth role in the Seahawks backfield going into the season.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) logs full practice Monday
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson remained a full participant in practice on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson remains on track to be good to go for Wednesday's season opener against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) practices in full Sunday
metadata.description: Emanuel Wilson was a full participant in practice on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Wilson enters the season in a depth role in the Seahawks backfield. He'll begin the year off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Emanuel Wilson Gets a Clean Bill of Health
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) was a full participant during practice on Sunday, according to Alex Barth of 98.5 The Sports Hub. Wilson dealt with a hamstring issue during the preseason, but the Seahawks' latest injury report confirms that he's fully healthy and will play in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, barring a setback. Seattle and New England face off on Wednesday to open the season, which is why their first injury report is coming out on a Sunday. As it stands, Wilson projects as the No. 3 running back behind Jadarian Price and George Holani. He might get a handful of touches in the season opener as the Seahawks figure out their backfield sans Zach Charbonnet (knee), but it probably won't be enough volume to get him on the fantasy radar in redraft leagues.
